_comment: Reward-per-unit-risk for a TP ladder, as BOTH implementations must compute it.
The arithmetic exists twice on purpose: backend/src/services/broker/ea_templates.py
ladder_rr() answers for anything server-side, and frontend/src/components/trading/
internal/ladderRr.ts answers while the operator is still typing in the EA template
editor, where a round trip per keystroke is not a readout, it is a lag.
Two implementations of one rule is exactly the thing this repo has been burned by,
so neither is allowed to be the reference: both are checked against the cases below.
the same cases through TypeScript. A change to one side that the other does not
follow fails on the side that did not move.
Every expected number here was worked out from the rule, not captured from a run:
rr = pips / sl; a level can only close what is still open (the EA's DoPartialClose
takes MathMin(lots, remaining)); and with close_full_on_last the deepest CONFIGURED
level banks whatever remains regardless of its own %.
levels are [level, pips, pct]; rows are [level, rr, closed_pct, contribution_r].
A level with pips <= 0 produces no row but still counts toward pct_sum and can

cases.why: The plain case: 50/30/20 over a 40-pip stop, each level closing exactly its own share.
25/25/25/100 sums to 175% and looks like 4.00R if the % column is summed. It banks 2.50R: TP4 can only take the 25% the earlier levels left.
close_full_on_last off, %s stopping at 70: 30% is genuinely left running on the trail.
One level at 50%. With the switch on it closes the whole position there, so the ladder is worth 1.00R and not 0.50R.
The same ladder with the switch off. The pair is what pins that the switch is read at all.
A level with a % but no distance is not a target. It produces no row, and TP2 is the last configured level, so it takes the lot.
R:R is reward over risk. With no stop there is no risk to divide by, and the answer is no answer rather than a number.
